title: BatteryFit Retrofit Pack

fingerprint.customer: Small Polish PV installers with existing prosumer customer bases and limited internal analysis capacity.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A PV customer asks whether a battery, EMS, or heat-storage retrofit is worth selling while net-billing, subsidy, OSD, and hardware-compatibility uncertainty create overpromise risk.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The installer pays 149-299 PLN per completed case or 1,500-3,000 PLN for a 10-case pilot after supplying a real customer intake.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A 24-48 hour concierge retrofit-qualification packet with conservative economics, compatibility notes, paperwork checks, alternatives, and do-not-sell flags; per-case or pilot service before software.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Family installer access, targeted outreach to small installers and wholesalers, then regional installer referrals.
fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A Polish retrofit-economics case set, maintained tariff/subsidy/OSD rules, hardware compatibility library, and observed conversion outcomes.

terminal_objection: No terminal rejection in the source; the principal caveat is that vendor or wholesaler tools can bundle the packet and the venture thesis fails without repeat paid use and measurable compliant-conversion improvement.
reopen_condition: Reconsider only with at least 3 paid or clearly committed installer pilots after 20 targeted outreaches and evidence that packets improve decisions or conversion without unacceptable liability/support burden.
scope_evidence: Approved and confirmed only as a validation target, not yet as a business.

title: PromoLeak Recovery Desk

fingerprint.customer: Polish 5-50M PLN challenger health, beauty, supplement, household, and FMCG brands selling through retailers, marketplaces, distributors, or modern trade.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Retailer deductions, promotion settlements, remittances, credit notes, or retail-media charges create suspected recoverable or preventable margin leakage.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The brand pays a 4,000-8,000 PLN fixed audit fee or 15-25% of cash recovered after granting access to real commercial documents.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A manual 14-day document-level recovery audit that identifies disputable deductions and unprofitable promotion mechanics; fixed-fee or success-fee service.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Evidence-led targeted outreach to qualified challenger brands, followed by referrals and repeat recovery/prevention work from proven cases.
fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A retailer- and agreement-specific deduction taxonomy, evidence patterns, dispute outcomes, promotion benchmarks, and prevention playbooks.

terminal_objection: No terminal rejection in the source; the decisive risk is that brands will not share sensitive documents or the first audits will not reveal material, evidence-backed leakage.
reopen_condition: Reconsider only when at least 2 brands share real documents under NDA or pay, and the first document-level audits identify at least 20k PLN per brand in recoverable or preventable leakage strong enough to dispute, reclaim, renegotiate, or change mechanics.
scope_evidence: Approved for validation only; the dossier requires access to real commercial documents and materially recoverable or preventable leakage.

title: CBAM Import Continuity Desk

fingerprint.customer: Polish customs brokers and freight forwarders handling repeated non-EU steel and aluminium imports for SME clients.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A shipment or importer relationship faces CBAM code, threshold, authorisation, supplier-evidence, default-value, or certificate-cost uncertainty that can disrupt import continuity.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: A broker pays 1,500-3,000 PLN for five branded memos or the importer pays 400-900 PLN for a follow-on continuity memo after document triage.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A manual broker-branded CBAM exposure and import-continuity memo from existing customs documents, sold as a pilot or per-case follow-on rather than software.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Targeted acquisition of customs brokers that already aggregate importer documents and can introduce multiple client cases.
fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Local CN/TARIC mappings, supplier-response history, Polish/English request templates, default-value exposure heuristics, case patterns, and broker trust.

terminal_objection: No terminal rejection in the source; the principal risk is that brokers will not provide real documents or introduce paying importers, while brokers, Big Four firms, or CBAM platforms can copy a generic memo layer.
reopen_condition: Reconsider only with at least 3 broker-led pilots using actual import documents or 2 paid importer follow-on packets; broker interest without document access does not qualify.
scope_evidence: Approved for validation only as a broker-first manual service.

title: Data Act Machine Data Liberation Desk

fingerprint.customer: Independent Polish compressed-air service firms and energy auditors serving manufacturing SMEs with 30-250 kW compressor rooms.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A named plant has suspected compressed-air waste but telemetry is locked or scattered and the service partner lacks data-backed evidence to sell an intervention.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The service partner pays 1,500-3,000 PLN per usable partner-branded savings memo or 5,000-9,000 PLN for a 3-5 memo pilot after customer-authorized retrieval.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Customer-authorized OEM/controller data retrieval plus a partner-branded commercial savings-evidence memo; manual per-case or pilot service with logger fallback.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Partner-led outreach to compressed-air service companies and energy auditors that already hold plant trust and can supply repeated cases.
fingerprint.compounding_advantage: OEM/controller access playbooks, authorization language, retrieval routes, savings-pattern data, intervention conversion evidence, and a local partner network.

terminal_objection: No terminal rejection in the source; the wedge collapses if partners cannot secure named-plant authorization and usable data, or if the work remains generic compressed-air auditing that OEMs and auditors can internalize.
reopen_condition: Reconsider only with at least 5 partners willing to introduce named authorized plants, at least 2 willing to pay or commit to 1,500-3,000 PLN follow-on memos, and at least 3 usable retrievals across the first 6 cases.
scope_evidence: Approved for validation only, not for product build or serious capital deployment.

title: GreenTender EPREL Bid Packs

fingerprint.customer: Polish lighting distributors, LED importers, and electrical wholesalers with public-sector tender exposure and 200-5,000 SKUs.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A live lighting tender has a deadline and the distributor cannot quickly map requirements to eligible SKUs and EPREL/product evidence without disqualification or a conservative no-bid.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The distributor pays 1,000-3,000 PLN for a 24-72 hour pack tied to one tender, with a possible 500-2,000 PLN monthly monitoring add-on.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A manual live-tender bid pack containing SKU match/reject lists, EPREL and label evidence, gaps, supplier questions, and a bid/no-bid recommendation; per-pack service plus optional monitoring.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Evidence-led outbound that names a public tender, relevant catalog items, and specific evidence gaps for each target distributor.
fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A Polish lighting tender-evidence graph linking requirement language, SKU aliases, private labels, EPREL registrants, supplier responses, and bid outcomes.

terminal_objection: No terminal rejection in the source; the main caveat is that the work can become bespoke consulting or be copied unless repeated tender/SKU/EPREL mappings and speed-to-bid improve with each engagement.
reopen_condition: Reconsider only if at least 2 targets pay or commit to the next live bid pack and the first 10 serious opportunities yield reusable mappings rather than bespoke expert work.
scope_evidence: The dossier records approval and independent confirmation gates without numeric scores.

title: Supplement Stack Safety & Lab-Response Passport

fingerprint.customer: Polish clinical dietitians, pharmacists, and small lab/wellness providers serving adults who take 5+ supplements and have recent labs.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A client presents a complex supplement stack, medication/context risks, and lab results that require duplication, dose, legitimacy, monitoring, and escalation reconciliation.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The end client pays 299-499 PLN for a reviewed case; the referring practitioner keeps 20-30% and reviewers receive fixed per-report fees.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A manual co-branded 6-10 page safety and lab-response passport with ingredient reconciliation, risk questions, monitoring gaps, and practitioner escalation; per-report service without affiliate sales.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Practitioner-led referrals and co-branded reports, with limited direct paid community sales used only as a demand test.
fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A normalized Polish product/ingredient/label and lab-marker graph, conservative review language, issue outcomes, and recurring practitioner relationships.

terminal_objection: No terminal rejection in the source; the main risks are medical/liability boundaries, reviewer and partner costs, practitioner self-provision, low willingness to pay, and a copyable report unless local data and referral trust compound.
reopen_condition: Reconsider only with at least 10 non-friend paid cases or 2 practitioners sending 3+ paid clients each, safe reviewer/legal boundaries, production trending below 90 minutes, viable gross margin, and reusable patterns from completed audits.
scope_evidence: Confirmed as a manual validation target only, not yet as a defensible software business.

title: HeatQuiet Noise Risk + Complaint Shield

fingerprint.customer: Premium Polish heat-pump installers plus distributor and warranty teams handling risky placements or actual complaints.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A proposed outdoor-unit site has boundary/window/night-noise risk, or an installed unit has triggered a neighbor, customer, warranty, or municipality complaint.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: An installer or channel pays 399-900 PLN per risky pre-install packet, 1,200-3,000 PLN per complaint triage, or for a multi-case pilot.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A manual Polish noise-risk and dispute-readiness evidence packet with placement options, missing evidence, mitigation, and qualified acoustic escalation; per-case or pilot service.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Family installer credibility, reconstructed local cases, targeted outreach to installers/distributors/warranty teams, and eventual embedding in a channel workflow.
fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A Polish siting-and-outcome risk graph by model, geometry, receiver, complaint, mitigation, expert escalation, channel workflow, and final resolution.

terminal_objection: No terminal rejection in the source; free calculators and acoustic consultants can satisfy the need, complaints may be too rare, and liability can force the product into generic certified acoustic consulting.
reopen_condition: Reconsider only with at least 3 paid pilots or one installer/distributor group pilot after 30 serious conversations, repeat channel usage, and an acoustic reviewer boundary that preserves a standardized workflow.
scope_evidence: Confirmed for validation, not for SaaS build or full company commitment.

title: BioSignal Claim-Risk Diligence Pack

fingerprint.customer: EU/CEE healthtech accelerators, venture studios, seed funds, and scout programs evaluating wearable, EEG, sleep, stress, recovery, or digital-biomarker startups.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A live investment or selection decision depends on whether an early-stage biosignal claim is credible enough before full clinical or regulatory proof exists.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The allocator pays 2,500-5,000 PLN for one live-deal memo or 10,000-20,000 PLN monthly for repeated screening.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A 72-hour fixed-format IC-ready claim-risk diligence memo with evidence gaps, confounders, claim boundaries, and decision-use recommendations; per-deal service or retainer.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Targeted private outreach using public teardown samples and evidence-request checklists, then referrals between funds, accelerators, and studios.
fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A private biosignal claim-risk benchmark graph, repeated IC language, evidence-request patterns, decision outcomes, and trusted reviewer relationships.

terminal_objection: No terminal rejection in the source; trust may belong to known regulatory, clinical, or CRO firms, the work can remain custom services, and the memo has no moat unless paid decision use produces repeated proprietary patterns.
reopen_condition: Reconsider only with 2 paid pilots or commitments, at least one memo used in a real decision workflow, sufficient NDA materials, viable reviewer margins, and recurring patterns across the first 5 paid memos.
scope_evidence: Confirmed only as a validation-stage business idea, not as a build decision.

title: REDBlocked Amazon Connected-Device Evidence Rescue Desk

fingerprint.customer: EU/CEE Amazon account-health, reinstatement, and compliance agencies serving private-label baby-monitor and indoor-camera sellers.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A live Amazon Seller Central request, ASIN suppression, CE/DoC rejection, RED/GPSR evidence gap, or supplier-document dispute blocks connected-device revenue.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The seller pays 2,000-3,000 PLN for request triage, 5,000-8,000 PLN for a full dossier, or 10,000-20,000 PLN for a multi-ASIN sprint while the agency retains 25-35%.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A white-label 48-72 hour Amazon evidence-response dossier with honest submit/cannot-submit boundaries, supplier RFI, response wording, and lab/notified-body escalation; fixed-fee case service.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Agencies already holding urgent seller relationships route live connected-device blocks to a specialist escalation desk.
fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Amazon request/evidence/outcome case memory, category-specific gaps, supplier responsiveness, lab routing, resolution timing, and agency referral quality.

terminal_objection: No terminal rejection in the source; threshold approval remained conditional because case frequency, reviewer cost, generic agency/lab substitution, and platform dependence can prevent a durable moat.
reopen_condition: Reconsider only through live blocked cases: at least 2 paid cases or commitments, 4 real case reviews, one two-way lab/CE partner, viable dossier economics, and reusable request/evidence/outcome patterns from the first cases.
scope_evidence: The dossier calls this a validation-stage pivot and requires live blocked cases rather than general interest.

title: DORA Bank Renewal Evidence Pack

fingerprint.customer: Polish/CEE 20-150 employee software-product vendors with 2-10 regulated financial customers and a live procurement or renewal blocker.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A bank, insurer, payment, leasing, or fintech buyer blocks a renewal or procurement on a DORA/ICT questionnaire, contract gap, subcontractor, audit-rights, exit-plan, or security evidence request.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The software vendor pays a fixed 12,000-24,000 PLN when a 100k+ PLN renewal, procurement, or strategic logo is actively at risk; later refreshes cost 6,000-12,000 PLN.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A fixed-scope seven-business-day vendor-side evidence index and buyer-ready response pack with cyber/legal issue splitting; paid rescue service plus annual refresh.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Highly targeted outbound to vendors with public finance customers plus referrals from boutique DORA, cyber, legal, ISO/SOC, and fractional-CISO partners.
fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A local bank-questionnaire-to-evidence map, accepted answer patterns, clause gaps, buyer pushback, versioned evidence snapshots, renewal deltas, and partner referrals.

terminal_objection: No terminal rejection in the source; the major caveats are trust, easy copying by cyber/legal/GRC advisors, time-windowed urgency, seven-day delivery risk, and drift into regulated advice or bespoke readiness work.
reopen_condition: Reconsider only with 3 paid pilots at 12k+ PLN from 40 qualified targets, at least 2 tied to urgent live deadlines, one repeatable partner referral source, and reusable question/evidence patterns from the first engagements.
scope_evidence: Approved only for validation, not for building a platform, hiring a team, or spending serious capital.

title: TraceFaktura All-Event Routing Pilot

fingerprint.customer: Private Polish municipal animal-care contractors serving at least 2-3 gminas with per-event or animal-level billing exposure.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Billable pickup, intake, transport, veterinary, shelter, or disposition events are captured in fragmented artifacts and later create invoice-prep labor, municipal questions, delayed acceptance, or audit/renewal anxiety.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The contractor prepays 3,000-5,000 PLN and pays 6,000-15,000 PLN for a 60-day all-event pilot, then potentially 1,000-3,000 PLN monthly.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A lightweight mandatory event-capture ledger that converts live animal-care events into gmina-specific invoice evidence and missing-field controls; prepaid pilot followed by subscription/per-event fees.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Precise outbound to contractors identified through public BIP, procurement, contract-award, program, and price-schedule evidence.
fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Accepted gmina packet rules, live event histories, missing-field logic, invoice-line conversion rules, staff habit, and contractor renewal/audit outcomes.

terminal_objection: The source explicitly says the control point remained contractual and behavioral rather than statutory, exclusive, a payment rail, or an official registry, leaving the idea below 85 and vulnerable to optional use or copyable forms.
reopen_condition: Reconsider only with a prepaid signed all-event routing mandate for at least two named gminas, written gmina format feedback, operational capture by non-founder staff, live events and invoice objects, and measurable reduction in reconstruction or questions.
verdict_evidence: Passed the user's revised validation threshold after the original gate was lowered to 82
scope_evidence: The dossier explicitly says the final score remained below 85.

title: Distributor-backed Heat-Pump Commissioning Passport

fingerprint.customer: Regional Polish heat-pump distributors, wholesalers, manufacturer representatives, warranty teams, and installer networks seeking quality control.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A retrofit job needs evidence before warranty fast-track, rebate, preferred procurement/status, installer ranking, or remediation because bad installations create callbacks, complaints, warranty friction, and brand damage.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The distributor or participating installer pays 100-300 PLN per job inside a written 10-job pilot tied to a real economic recognition gate.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A pass/risk/rework commissioning passport from job photos, design assumptions, settings, handover evidence, and risk flags; per-job workflow tied to channel economics.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Founder family-company case access leads to one local distributor/wholesaler pilot and later installer/channel network adoption.
fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A Polish retrofit-risk and outcome dataset linking installation design, equipment match, expectations, callbacks, warranty disputes, bill disappointment, and distributor resolution.

terminal_objection: No terminal rejection in the source; without written distributor recognition, installers see only paperwork and a manufacturer, CRM, or installer can copy the checklist without losing an economic gate.
reopen_condition: Reconsider only with a written 10-job distributor pilot that recognizes the passport for warranty speed, rebate eligibility, installer ranking, preferred status, or another real economic gate, plus evidence that scoring predicts outcomes.
scope_evidence: Confirmed only as a validation target; the recorded kill condition is no written 10-job distributor pilot with real economic recognition.

title: CarrierProof DPD/DHL Recovery Rail

fingerprint.customer: One mid-sized Polish ecommerce 3PL serving fashion and beauty merchants with recurring DPD/DHL parcel exceptions.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A stream of lost or damaged parcels goes under-recovered because deadlines, evidence, triage, appeals, and reconciliation are fragmented or treated as support overhead.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The founder earns a success fee only from recovered cash or carrier credits after the 3PL and merchants delegate a routed pilot claim lane.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A no-upfront revenue-share recovery rail for a narrow 3PL merchant cohort and claim classes, combining historical review, evidence triage, filing, appeals, and settlement tracking.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: One 3PL channel grants access to many merchants and routes an exclusive exception stream instead of merchant-by-merchant sales.
fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Carrier- and claim-specific eligibility, evidence, rejection, appeal, payout, and labor data that improves expected-value triage and recovery performance.

terminal_objection: The real working-chat gate failed because contractual control is revocable, the 3PL or a claims vendor can internalize the workflow, per-claim value may be too small, delegation is messy, and the concept becomes an admin service without exclusivity and routed flow.
reopen_condition: Reconsider only after one 3PL routes claims by SOP, at least 10 merchants authorize, 50 cases are screened, 25 evidence-complete claims are submitted, 10-15 recoveries are paid or approved, labor economics improve, and the partner expands or deepens the mandate.
scope_evidence: The dossier explicitly says the idea does not currently qualify as confirmed.

title: BioWear Regulated-Listing Ticket-Book Buyout

fingerprint.customer: A small marketplace/account-health or compliance agency with connected-wearable evidence tickets; end payers are wellness, sleep, recovery, baby-monitoring, or biosignal wearable sellers.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A live Amazon/Allegro CE, GPSR, RED cyber, app/data, label/manual, claim-boundary, or supplier-document request blocks listing, payments, ads, shipment, or inventory.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Sellers prepay through a documented agency split after an exclusive 6-12 month routing option assigns live regulated-product tickets.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Acquire or option an agency's regulated connected-wearable ticket lane, execute assigned evidence cases with reviewers/labs, and monetize prepaid case work.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Exclusive agency routing and inherited ticket/support history replace cold seller acquisition.
fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Assigned case-flow plus a case-memory database of request types, supplier defects, evidence, response wording, reviewer/lab routing, and channel outcomes.

terminal_objection: The real gate found ticket-flow control fragile rather than hard, the agency profile possibly rare, agencies able to copy, platform and supplier dependencies unresolved, case frequency uncertain, and the concept insufficiently distinct from REDBlocked.
reopen_condition: Reconsider only with one signed exclusive 6-12 month routing agreement, at least 3 assigned live tickets, 2 paying clients, 25,000+ PLN prepaid, a real channel submission, contracted reviewers, 60%+ gross margin, and a demonstrably distinct reusable case-memory asset.
scope_evidence: The dossier treats this as an unconfirmed adjacent expansion/acquisition variant of REDBlocked.

title: HeritageDoor Suites

fingerprint.customer: Premium interior architects, heritage renovators, boutique developers, property managers, and joiners working on Polish pre-war projects.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A premium renovation needs architectural continuity but complete matching internal-door sets are fragmented, damaged, scrapped, or sold as singles before the project buyer can secure them.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: A project gatekeeper pays a 2,000-10,000 PLN reservation deposit and later buys a controlled raw/prepped suite for 8,000-25,000 PLN or a partner-restored package for 20,000-60,000+ PLN.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Acquire or option complete 4-12 door matched suites with measurements, condition, hardware, reservation, and restorer handoff; inventory-spread business rather than sourcing advice.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Upstream first-refusal and fast-pickup relationships with demolition, clear-out, renovation, salvage, and administrator channels, paired with concrete-suite outreach to 120 renovation gatekeepers.
fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Physical inventory control, first-look supplier density, removal reputation, suite condition/profile data, gatekeeper demand memory, and repeat restorer/architect habits.

terminal_objection: No terminal rejection in the source; passage was narrow because demand may be thin, fit/fire/acoustic/restoration issues can block projects, storage and damage consume capital, and control expires if suppliers split suites before calling.
reopen_condition: Reconsider only with 3 written first-refusal or pickup agreements, 3 physically controlled matched suites, 3 paid full-suite deposits, one paid handoff, and at least one suite showing greater than 50% gross margin before founder salary.
scope_evidence: The dossier's proof gate requires control of three matched suites and three paid deposits from real project gatekeepers.
